_comment: Hand-authored descriptions merged into docs/DATABASE_REFERENCE.md by scripts/export-schema-doc.mjs. Structure, types, keys and row counts come from the live database; only the prose lives here. Keyed by relation, then column.

layers.reference: Layer 1 — reference. Slow-moving facts that everything else points at.
layers.source-mirror: Layer 2 — source mirror. What the storefront literally says, stored before any interpretation.
layers.canonical: Layer 3 — canonical. What we derive: the paddle hierarchy reconciled across storefronts that model it differently.
layers.vocabulary: Vocabulary. Controlled value lists, referenced by foreign key so adding a brand's new word is an INSERT rather than a migration.
layers.timeseries: Time series. Append-only history. These are the only tables that accumulate; everything else is overwritten in place each crawl.
layers.reviews: Reviews. Customer text, brand replies, and the per-run aggregate that makes sentiment-over-time a range scan.
layers.ops: Operations. Crawl bookkeeping — which run wrote what, and what failed.

brands.purpose: One row per brand. The top of the ownership chain: a site belongs to a brand, and everything else hangs off a site.

columns.slug: URL-safe identifier, e.g. `joola`. Unique. This is what `?brand=` carries in the dashboard.
columns.name: Display name as the brand writes it, e.g. `JOOLA`.

countries.purpose: ISO country list with a default currency, so a storefront in a new market does not invent its own code.

columns.name: Display name.
columns.currency: ISO-4217 default for the market, e.g. `USD`. A site may override it.

sites.purpose: One row per (brand, country) storefront. This is the crawl target, and the unit that country expansion adds rows to — the same paddle sold in the US and Australia belongs to two sites.

columns.assortment_handles: Which source collections make up the assortment we care about. Declared in `src/config/` and mirrored here so a query can explain why a product was crawled.
columns.is_active: Excluded from scheduled crawls when false.
columns.crawl_delay_ms: Politeness delay between requests. Raised where robots.txt asks for it.
columns.notes: Free text for whoever onboarded the site.
columns.review_platform: `bazaarvoice` | `okendo` | `judgeme` | null. Selects the review adapter. A NULL here is why a brand silently collects zero reviews.
columns.review_config: Credentials the review adapter needs — Bazaarvoice client and displayCode, Okendo subscriberId, Judge.me shop domain. Config, not schema, so brand #4 stays a config change.

players.purpose: Endorsing athletes. Colourways on some brands are named after players (`Blaze Red (Ben Johns)`), which makes the player a real analytic dimension rather than a string in a title.

columns.name: Display name.
columns.slug: URL-safe identifier, unique within the brand.

technologies.purpose: Brand technology dictionary — `Carbon Friction Surface`, `Propulsion Core`. Currently empty: the PDP stage that would populate it has never run.

columns.name: Marketing name as published.
columns.slug: URL-safe identifier, unique within the brand.
columns.description: Long-form explanation where the brand publishes one.
columns.first_seen_at: First crawl that saw this technology named.

product_lines.purpose: A family of paddles carried across generations — `Perseus`, `VANGUARD`, `SLK`.

columns.slug: URL-safe identifier, e.g. `perseus`. Unique within the brand.
columns.name: Display name, e.g. `Perseus`.

generations.purpose: A brand's version marker — `Gen 1`, `Pro IV`, `Pro V`, `3S`. Separated from the line so `Perseus Pro V` can be compared with `Perseus Pro IV`.

columns.name: Display name, e.g. `Pro V`.
columns.sequence: Ordering for "which version is newer": Gen 1 = 1, Pro IV = 4, Pro V = 5. NULL where the brand publishes no ordering.

models.purpose: The reconciled paddle: line x generation x optional sub-line. This is the unit a person means by "a paddle", and the level at which two brands can be compared.

columns.product_line_id: Line this model belongs to. NULL where the line could not be resolved.
columns.generation_id: Generation marker. NULL where the line carries no generation designation.
columns.sub_line: Variant of the line — `Dual`, `CFS`, or NULL.
columns.slug: URL-safe identifier, e.g. `perseus-pro-v`. Unique within the brand.
columns.name: Display name, e.g. `Perseus Pro V`.
columns.shape: FK to `shapes`. **Currently `unknown` on every row** — nothing rolls the variant shapes up into it. Read `v_model_overview.shapes` (aggregated from the variants) instead.
columns.play_style: FK to `play_styles`. `power` | `control` | `hybrid` | `unknown`. Selkirk merchandises this as a first-class dimension; JOOLA does not use it at all, which is why the default is `unknown`.
columns.updated_at: Maintained by the `models_touch` trigger on every update.

notes: `shape` is dead weight today: all 80 rows say `unknown`, because the value is never derived from the variants that do carry a shape. The catalogue page reads the aggregated `shapes` array from `v_model_overview` instead.

categories.purpose: Collections and menu nodes as published by the site. Self-referencing, so the mega-menu tree survives intact.

columns.source_category_id: The platform's own id, e.g. a Shopify collection id. Unique per site.
columns.title: Display title, e.g. `Pro`.
columns.parent_id: Parent collection, for the menu tree.
columns.depth: Depth in that tree; 0 is top level.
columns.category_role: FK to `category_roles`. Derived: what this collection *means*, which drives the UI's facet grouping.
columns.in_main_nav: Whether it appears in the primary navigation.
columns.product_count: Count the storefront claims for this collection.
columns.last_seen_at: Most recent crawl that saw it.
columns.is_active: False once the collection stops appearing.

products.purpose: One row per product per site. The same physical paddle sold in two markets is two rows — that is intentional, because price, stock and reviews differ per market.

columns.model_id: Canonical model, resolved during the normalize stage. NULL until resolution succeeds.
columns.source_product_id: The platform's own product id. Unique per site.
columns.title: Listing title as published.
columns.product_type: Product type field from the platform.
columns.tags: Platform tags. GIN-indexed; a source of derived attributes.
columns.is_in_assortment: **The assortment gate.** Accessories and apparel slip into paddle collections; every analytic query filters on this. Note it is applied in application code, not inside the views.
columns.first_seen_at: First crawl that saw the listing.
columns.last_seen_at: Most recent crawl that saw it.
columns.is_active: False once the listing stops appearing.

product_categories.purpose: Which collections a product sits in, over time. Carries first/last seen rather than being a plain join table, because a product entering the `Sale` collection is a signal in its own right.

columns.product_id: Product. Half of the composite primary key.
columns.category_id: Collection. Other half of the composite primary key.
columns.first_seen_at: First crawl that saw this membership.
columns.last_seen_at: Most recent crawl that saw it.
columns.is_active: False once the product leaves the collection.

variants.purpose: The SKU — the atomic unit of the price and stock time series. Raw option values are kept exactly as the source gave them, so a normalization bug is always recoverable without a re-crawl.

columns.site_id: Storefront, denormalised so snapshots can filter without a join.
columns.source_variant_id: The platform's own variant id. Unique per site.
columns.title: Variant title as published, e.g. `16mm / Blaze Red (Ben Johns)`.
columns.option1_name: Raw option label as the source gave it, e.g. `Thickness`.
columns.endorsed_player_id: Derived. FK to `players` when the colourway is named after an athlete.
columns.shape: Derived. FK to `shapes`. This is the field that actually carries shape data — the model-level column does not.
columns.attr_source: Which input won for each derived attribute, e.g. `{"core_thickness_mm":"title"}`. Candidates are option value, title, tag, collection, PDP, LLM or manual.
columns.attr_confidence: 0.00-1.00, the lowest confidence across the derived attributes on this row.
columns.attributes: Long-tail specs that do not deserve a column of their own.
columns.first_seen_at: First crawl that saw the SKU.
columns.last_seen_at: Most recent crawl that saw it.
columns.is_active: False once the SKU stops appearing.

product_content.purpose: PDP-derived copy and specs, versioned by content hash so a re-crawl that changed nothing writes no row. **Empty** — the stage that fills it has never been run.

columns.content_hash: SHA-256 of the normalised payload. Unique per product, and the mechanism that suppresses no-op rows.
columns.specs: Spec table as published, e.g. `{'Core':'16mm Polypropylene'}`.
columns.technologies: Technology names named on the page.
columns.media: Images and video referenced by the PDP.

product_technologies.purpose: Which technologies a product claims, over time. **Empty**, because `technologies` is empty.

columns.product_id: Product. Half of the composite primary key.
columns.first_seen_at: First crawl that saw the claim.
columns.last_seen_at: Most recent crawl that saw it.
columns.is_active: False once the claim disappears from the product.

skill_tiers.purpose: Controlled list behind `models.skill_tier`. Replaced a CHECK constraint so a brand shipping an unfamiliar tier word is an INSERT over the REST API, not a migration a human has to paste into a dashboard.

columns.code: Stored value, e.g. `pro`. Primary key, referenced by FK.
columns.label: Display label, e.g. `Pro`.

category_roles.purpose: Controlled list behind `categories.category_role` — what a collection means, as opposed to what it is called.

crawl_runs.purpose: One row per crawl. Everything a run writes carries its `run_id`, so a bad run can be identified, explained and excluded from charts.

columns.id: Run id. Stamped onto every row the run writes.
columns.status: `pending` | `running` | `done` | `partial` | `error`. A run stuck at `running` means `finaliseRun()` was rejected.
columns.stages_done: Stages that completed. The gap between the two is the pipeline-health panel.
columns.products_new: Listings seen for the first time.
columns.variants_new: SKUs seen for the first time.
columns.stats: Whole `RunStats` object. Every stat also needs a column here or the finalising update is rejected.
columns.error_message: Failure detail where the run did not complete.
columns.finished_at: Run end. NULL while running, or if the run never finalised.
columns.reviews_found: Reviews fetched this run. **Counts fetched rows, not inserted ones** — it overstates when a crawl re-reads reviews it already holds.
columns.reviews_new: Reviews seen for the first time. Subject to the same overcount.
columns.review_responses_new: Brand replies seen for the first time.

notes: `reviews_found` / `reviews_new` count what was fetched rather than what was inserted. One Selkirk run logged 13,136 against 5,777 rows actually stored.

crawl_errors.purpose: One row per failure inside a run, so a partial crawl can be explained without reading logs.

columns.target: The URL or handle that failed.
columns.status_code: HTTP status where the failure was a response.

variant_snapshots.purpose: Append-only. One row per SKU per successful run — the table the whole project exists for. A failed run writes no snapshots, so a site outage can never be mistaken for a catalogue-wide stockout.

columns.site_id: Storefront, denormalised so site-wide range scans need no join.
columns.observed_at: **When we looked — not when the price changed.** Charts must step-interpolate between points, never linearly interpolate.
columns.compare_at_price: Struck-through reference price, where the storefront publishes one.
columns.discount_pct: Generated, stored: percentage off, rounded to 2dp, else 0. Stored so "everything over 20% off on any past date" is an index scan rather than a scan plus arithmetic.
columns.is_available: In stock at that moment. NULL where the storefront does not say.
columns.inventory_quantity: Units on hand. NULL when not exposed, which is most of the time.
columns.position_in_category: Merchandising position within the primary collection. Movement here is an early signal of a push or a wind-down.

notes: Unique on `(run_id, variant_id)`, which guards against double-writing a SKU inside one run.
Indexed with BRIN on `observed_at` — tiny, and the right shape for an append-only time-ordered column.
Sizing note from the migration: at roughly 10M rows this should become a monthly-partitioned table. Only the pipeline and the views read it directly, so that stays a contained change.

variant_events.purpose: The derived change log, written by the diff stage by comparing a run against the previous successful one. Everything here is recomputable from `variant_snapshots`; it exists so "what changed" needs no window functions over the full history.

columns.context: Extra detail for the event type.

notes: Only 1 row exists: a change needs two observations to sit between, and the crawl has not run often enough to produce more.

reviews.purpose: One row per customer review, ever. Upserted on its source id rather than re-inserted per run, because a review's text is written once — but the things around it (helpful counts, brand replies) do move.

columns.site_id: Storefront the review was left on.
columns.product_id: The listing it is attached to. **Exactly one**, even for a review syndicated across a paddle's twelve colourway listings — see the known limitation below.
columns.review_platform: `bazaarvoice` | `okendo` | `judgeme`. Part of the natural key, because source ids collide across platforms.
columns.source_review_id: The platform's own id. Unique within `(site_id, review_platform)`.
columns.rating: Stars. numeric, not integer, because Okendo can emit halves.
columns.title: Review headline. Weighted above body in the search vector.
columns.pros: Structured pros where the platform collects them separately.
columns.author_name: Display name only — whatever the storefront already shows in public.
columns.author_location: Free-text location. Arrives as a nested object on Okendo and is flattened on ingest.
columns.is_incentivized: Review was given in exchange for something.
columns.is_syndicated: Platform marked it as syndicated from elsewhere.
columns.is_ratings_only: A star with no words. These must count toward the average but must never surface as an empty card in a text search.
columns.helpful_count: Current helpful votes, refreshed each run.
columns.variant_label: Which SKU the reviewer bought, as the platform labels it.
columns.context_data: Platform-specific structured extras kept whole rather than flattened — Bazaarvoice Age / Gender / LengthOfOwnership, secondary ratings, badges. Raw material for later sentiment work.
columns.source_updated_at: Last edit timestamp from the platform.
columns.first_seen_at: When we first saw it. The gap from `submitted_at` is our own collection lag.
columns.last_seen_at: Most recent crawl that saw it.
columns.first_seen_run_id: Run that first stored it. Drives the arrival-rate metric.
columns.last_seen_run_id: Most recent run that saw it.
columns.language_code: Language where the platform reports one.
columns.search_tsv: Generated, stored tsvector. Title weighted A, body B, pros/cons C, so `cracked` in a headline outranks it in a paragraph. GIN-indexed.

notes: Unique on `(site_id, review_platform, source_review_id)` — `product_id` is deliberately *not* in that key, because one customer's opinion syndicated across twelve colourway listings is one opinion, not twelve.

The consequence is the known limitation: the row can carry only one `product_id`, so filtering by any other listing the review appears under finds nothing. 26 listings hold no reviews of their own for this reason.
A partial index on `(site_id, submitted_at desc) where rating <= 3` backs the most expensive common query, "show me the complaints".

review_responses.purpose: The brand reply chain. No platform guarantees a stable id for a reply, so the dedupe key is a hash of the body — replies are edited rarely, and an edited reply is genuinely a new thing to have seen.

columns.source_response_id: Platform's id where it provides one. Often NULL.
columns.response_hash: SHA-256 of the normalised body. Unique per review, and the actual dedupe key.
columns.response_source: Which endpoint it came from, e.g. `mc-api`.
columns.first_seen_at: When we first saw the reply.
columns.last_seen_at: Most recent crawl that saw it.

notes: All 744 rows belong to JOOLA and Selkirk. CRBN has zero — verified against the source: all 24 CRBN products render an empty `jdgm-rev__reply` container, so the brand writes no replies at all.

product_review_snapshots.purpose: Append-only, one row per product per run. The series that answers the question the feature exists for: how a product's reception changes over months. Deliberately denormalised into star buckets so a distribution chart is one row, not a group-by over every review ever written.

columns.reported_total: What the platform itself claims its total is. Kept apart from our own count so a truncated crawl is visible rather than silent.
columns.review_count: Rows we actually hold for this listing.
columns.with_text_count: Of those, how many carry words.
columns.ratings_only_count: Of those, how many are stars alone.
columns.new_review_count: Reviews whose `first_seen_run_id` is this run — the arrival rate, which leads the average. A drop to zero on a product that averaged ten a week is worth knowing well before the average moves.

notes: Summing `review_count` across this table double-counts syndicated reviews: it records the platform's number for *every* listing a review appears under. It claims 24,911 placements over 14,840 actual reviews. Use `v_review_brand_counts` / `v_review_product_counts` for counts that match what clicking a filter returns.

Holds 4 rows against 7 migration files. Migrations 0005, 0006 and 0007 were applied by hand through the Supabase SQL editor, which does not write this ledger, so it understates what the database actually has.

v_variant_current.purpose: Current state of every SKU: the newest snapshot joined through to the canonical model. The workhorse for catalogue browsing.

derived.observed_at: From the newest `variant_snapshots` row for the SKU, via a LATERAL join.

notes: Returns all 361 SKUs. It does **not** apply the `is_in_assortment` gate — application code does that ([queries.ts:161](../src/lib/queries.ts#L161)), which is why the dashboard shows 346.

v_model_overview.purpose: One row per model with its SKUs rolled up — the catalogue table's source.

derived.shapes: Distinct variant shapes excluding `unknown`. **This is the real shape data** — `models.shape` is `unknown` everywhere.
derived.price_min: Lowest current price across the model's SKUs.

notes: Filters `where vc.is_in_assortment`, so it returns 76 of the 80 rows in `models`.

v_active_discounts.purpose: Every in-assortment SKU currently on sale, deepest discount first.
notes: Filters on `is_on_sale and is_in_assortment`; ordered by `discount_pct desc`.

v_recent_changes.purpose: The change feed — `variant_events` joined to the names a reader needs, newest first. Carries `brand_slug` so the dashboard can scope without a join.

v_variant_price_daily.purpose: Daily OHLC-style rollup of the price series, one row per SKU per UTC day.

derived.was_on_sale: True if on sale at any point that day.
derived.was_available: True if in stock at any point that day.
derived.was_always_available: True only if in stock at every observation that day.
derived.observations: How many times we looked that day.

v_category_tree.purpose: The collection tree with parent titles and active product counts resolved.

derived.active_products: Count of active `product_categories` rows for the collection.

v_review_search.purpose: One row per review, pre-joined to everything the search page filters on, so the UI never fans out joins per row.
notes: 14,840 rows — one per review, no duplication.

v_product_reviews_current.purpose: Latest review standing per product: the aggregate shown next to price on catalogue and model pages.
notes: 142 rows — one per *product*, including the 42 that have no snapshot (LEFT JOIN LATERAL), so it is not a list of products that have reviews.

v_review_product_counts.purpose: One row per product that genuinely has reviews stored against it. Counts the `reviews` table itself rather than the snapshots.
notes: 100 rows, against 126 listings that the snapshots claimed had reviews. The 26 missing are the syndication casualties.
Added by migration 0007 to make a filter chip's number and the result of clicking it the same number.

v_review_brand_counts.purpose: One row per brand, counting distinct stored reviews — the number behind each brand chip.
notes: CRBN 6,202 · Selkirk 6,161 · JOOLA 2,477, summing to the 14,840 rows in `reviews`.
